subject: Intermittent 5xx/timeouts observed for Atlas-7b — customer notice and recovery plan
messages:
From: monitoring@redwood.com
To: platform-ops@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-24T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate for model=atlas-7b in us-west-2

Automated alert:
- Service: inference-runtime/us-west-2
- Model: atlas-7b
- Symptom: spike in 5xx (primarily 503 + upstream timeouts) starting 2027-06-24T07:58:00Z
- Current 5xx rate: 4.6% (baseline 0.1%)
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (chat + completion) for model alias atlas-7b-prod

First responders: dylan_brooks, marissa_cole.
Action: triage on-call and open incident ticket.
[attachment: atlas-7b-500-samples-20270624.log (text/plain)]

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: sara.thomas@brightlanehealth.com, ops@brightlanehealth.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-24T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Quick notice: degraded responses from Atlas‑7b (possible 5xx/timeouts) — we're on it

Hi Sara / BrightLane Ops team,

We wanted to let you know we have detected intermittent 5xx responses and increased request timeouts for the Atlas-7b model that may affect calls routed to atlas-7b-prod in the US region. Our monitoring shows degraded success rate beginning ~07:58 UTC.

What we know so far:
- Impact: a subset of generation calls are returning 503 or timing out; success rate has dropped to ~95% in short bursts.
- Scope: a portion of BrightLane traffic routed to atlas-7b-prod may be affected (we're seeing some of your calls in the error samples).
- Immediate action: our infra + runtime teams are investigating kernel-level regressions and autoscaler behaviour; we have opened INC-2027-0624-ATLAS.

Near-term mitigation we're applying:
- Rolling traffic fallback to atlas-7b-quant (compatible variant) for latency-sensitive routes where acceptable.
- Increased autoscaler headroom in the affected AZs.
- Rate-limited retries from our edge for idempotent requests.

We will follow up with a short update in ~60 minutes and a fuller post-incident summary once we have root cause. If you see specific customer-impacting failures (request ids or timestamps), please reply with the examples and we'll correlate immediately.

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing recovery.

-evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
[attachment: ma-runbook-20270624.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: sara.thomas@brightlanehealth.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: ops@brightlanehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-24T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick notice: degraded responses from Atlas‑7b (possible 5xx/timeouts) — we're on it

Thanks Evelyn — we are seeing increased error rates in our ingestion pipeline starting ~08:05 UTC and a handful of failed user requests. Sample request IDs: req_34b2, req_34b7, req_351a.

Priority: this affects a scheduled clinical triage feature so any ETA on a mitigation would be helpful. We prefer avoiding model substitution for clinical generation without validation; if you must route to atlas-7b-quant please let us run a quick sanity check first.

We appreciate the quick heads-up.

— Sara
Sara Thomas
Head of Integrations, BrightLane Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-24T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/timeouts observed for Atlas-7b — customer notice and recovery plan

Quick internal status:
- Triage summary: hitting a combination of kernel-side memory churn and a degraded KV cache hit rate causing longer tail latency. Autoscaler did spin, but scale-up lag combined with connection retries amplified 503s.
- Mitigations applied at 09:00 UTC: forced roll to atlas-7b-quant for brightlane routes (per Evelyn's plan) but flagged as opt-in; we have not diverted critical clinical routes without approval.
- ETA for stabilization: ~30–90 minutes depending on warm cache convergence.

Next steps:
1) Patch: reconfigure allocator to reduce memory churn (in-flight).
2) Ops: force-increase min-size for affected pool in us-west-2 for 2 hours.
3) Customer comms: Evelyn to propose rollback options and discuss safe validation windows with BrightLane.

I'll keep the incident ticket updated (INC-2027-0624-ATLAS).
— Marissa

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: sara.thomas@brightlanehealth.com, ops@brightlanehealth.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, tim.watson@cloudpartnerships.io
Date: 2027-06-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Recovery confirmed and follow-up: Atlas‑7b incident (INC-2027-0624-ATLAS)

Hi Sara — quick update and postmortem notes now that we've stabilized: 

What changed / resolution:
- Root cause: elevated memory churn in a newly rolled kernel optimization interacting poorly with our KV cache eviction policy under a bursty request mix. This increased tail latency and led to transient 503s.
- Fixes deployed: we reverted the kernel optimization, tuned cache eviction thresholds, and temporarily increased min instance pool size for the atlas-7b-prod fleet.
- Recovery: success rate returned to baseline by 2027-06-24T12:42:00Z; we removed forced routing fallback at 2027-06-24T13:10:00Z.

Impact to BrightLane: your clinical triage feature experienced intermittent failures between ~08:05–12:40 UTC on 2027-06-24. We correlated the sample request IDs you provided and confirmed failures were within that window.

Preventive actions (next steps):
- We will ship a defensive guard in the allocator to prevent the specific churn pattern — target release: 2027-07-02.
- Add a model-level canary policy for kernel changes (gradual canary + live traffic shadowing for 48 hours) — target: 2027-07-05.
- We will provide you a short validation window to allow BrightLane to approve fallbacks (if any) prior to automatic routing changes.

We will send a concise post-incident report with timelines, logs, and code references by 2027-06-28. If you have any follow-ups or want a quick sync, I'm available this week for a 20-minute call.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for the prompt examples — they helped us triage faster.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
